comment: The verdict paths of the Lean service (docs/spec/kernel-boundary.md, section 2). tier kernel: the path's answers may carry a verdict and its spec and wrap lines count toward the kernel total; tier candidate: measured, not yet admitted. entry: the right-hand side of the mode's runMode_* pin; theorems: what an accepted answer means; subject: the runner or decision the theorems are about (not read): some listed theorem must state its answer (`subject … = .ok answer` with the answer used, or `subject … = true`), or the tool reports it; delegates: entries of other paths this entry hands cases to; nonverdict: exits reviewed as carrying no verdict, each with its reason. uncovered (kernel paths): code a subject runs for case kinds no listed theorem covers, with the kinds and the reason; it is outside the kernel (every kernel path's spec and census body is cut there; the tool reports one a kernel spec or wrap still reaches) and its verdict writers count outside. covered_writers (kernel paths): each verdict writer that is inside the kernel only because a subject runs it, with the case kinds it writes for and the listed theorems that cover them; an unnamed one is reported. Measured by tools/kernel_closure.py; only the architect seat changes a tier. imports: modules that hold a listed theorem and are imported only by VE.Audit (build them first: lake build <module>). kinds (kernel paths): every case kind the path's runners compare with the case's `kind`, mapped to {"theorem": a listed theorem whose statement fixes that kind} or {"nonverdict": why the answer carries no verdict}. untied_kinds: verdict-bearing kinds of a kernel path that no theorem in lean/statements.txt states (with `family`, a family the kind's theorem does not cover; `near`, theorems about a part of the answer's computation, not about the answer).

keys.comment: The Lean code under the five frozen keys' answers (docs/kernel/frozen-keys-20261111.md): the spec and wrap of every path whose mode the keys call, and the validators the keys call, counted in full (their whole run closure). Measured as keyed_lines; keyed_kernel_lines is the part inside the kernel.

validator_roles.comment: What each validator is to the verdict paths the keys call (decision D13, kb-validators; docs/kernel/kb-validators/REPORT.md). A pre-filter of a path: the path checks the same inputs itself, so a wrong "ok" from the validator changes none of that path's verdicts. A translator: a value of its answer is carried into later cases or shown, and no path checks it.

check.note: each of the three re-types its formulas; quantity re-elaborates the W6 statement and binds its meaning ids. The `Q` and `core` a check answer gives Python are counted as translations in the report's part 2 (iii), not here.

model.note: since kb-validators: metered applies the norms profile check itself (VE.Route.MeteredRun.profiled, the model mode's Plain.profileOkOn) and runWith_sound states it (ProfileAdmits).

environment.note: not a pre-filter: Python stores its canonical `acts` in place of the authored act texts and sends them in every later case (ve/backends/validation.py:85-105, ve/environment.py:225-226); counted under the keys until the architect seat rules on part 2 (ii).

uncovered.name: VE.SoftNorms.Run.runSoftKind
uncovered.why: every soft kind but admission: soft-certificate answers `valid`, soft-conflict CONFLICT or CONFLICT-FREE, soft-elaborate a `soft_status` of CHECKED (residualStatus); soft_wire_acceptance and runAdmission_sound cover admission, soft_wire_elaborate states only the background and premises fields of soft-elaborate, not its soft_status (KB-3), soft_wire_selected covers soft-selected (its whole answer; kb-10a), and slot_wire_certificate and slot_wire_conflict cover slot-certificate and slot-conflict (their whole answers over the slot replays; kb-3), which are therefore not listed here

nonverdict.name: VE.Route.MeteredTrace.document

nonverdict.name: VE.Time.Wire.runCount

nonverdict.name: VE.Time.Wire.runConversion
